If you don't mind a few tips...

1) Encode it to mp3 or ogg at 64 kbps. This will cut the file size down to a tenth of the size, if not more. If you plan to put music in the background, then I would up the bitrate to 96 kbps.

2) Read, reread, and rereread the posts you are going to read before you record so you know better what you're going to say. It's clear that you are reading when recording because there no emotion in your voice. Without emotion it will sound forced and not interesting.

3) The swipes are a nice touch but without telling the user at the beginning they won't know what the point of them are. I would include a disclaimer at the start and say something quick like, "as a reminder, the swipe (play the sound) signifies a topic change. And with that, let's get to the posts."

4) Another option, instead of using swipes, if you had background music playing, you can put a 2-3 second pause between topics and increase the volume of the song in that period. The pause in dialog and increased volume of the music is a natural way for the listener to understand that something different is coming next. As for the music, that's up to you, but I've always been a fan of getting some creative commons licensed downtempo, or instrumental trip-hop songs.

That video is good advice, but that's not what emotion is, or, maybe I'm using the wrong description, idk, but let me explain.

When you apply emotion to your speech, you will be placing emphasis on certain words. That emphasis can change the overall meaning or intent of what you are trying to convey to the listener. A great way to illustrate what I mean is think about when you are trying to explain something to someone who, despite all efforts, doesn't get it and you keep trying to explain that thing but you are getting frustrated. You will start to emphasize different words, there will be a slight vibrato in your voice to show anger or disdain.

If you have never had to show emotion before it is a very difficult thing to change. It's effectively trying to change your behavior. Doing something you normally never did before. But, practice is the best thing to do.
